profile.headline: Software Engineer at Meta | Computer Science (B.A.) at University of California, Berkeley
profile.summary:
I am a software engineer with years of industry experience in full-stack development. I graduated with a bachelor's degree in computer science from the University of California, Berkeley (UC Berkeley).

As a resourceful software engineer, I am proficient in C#, Python, Java, SQL, and JavaScript; I am familiar with scheme, C++, and Matlab through classes I took at Berkeley and have the savvy of good programming practices through industry training and experience. I have implemented projects written in Python that include object-oriented programming (OOP), unit testing, and complexity analysis. My personal work can be found on my Github, https://github.com/ranellegomez/. If you are interested in seeing my schoolwork from Berkeley, please ask, and I will happily share. I am communicative, determined, and resourceful, and I deploy these traits in my work and personal life. 

My passions include photographing scenery (please see cover photo) and people; My works have been recognized by UC Berkeley (i.e., featured front-page on berkeley.edu), ABC7 Los Angeles, and South Bay Photos. 

Interested? Let’s talk! Please do not hesitate to contact me by the following mediums.
Email: ranellegomez@gmail.com 
Phone call or text message: (323) 999-4720

positions.locationName: Greater Los Angeles Area and San Francisco Bay Area
positions.description:
I served clients of various product needs (i.e., weddings, graduations, professional headshots, events, engagements, architecture), established a legal logistical contract for photographer-client relations (e.g., pricing, timeframes, locations, guaranteed number of proofs and edits),  provided 600 photo proofs within a one-day-average return period, and delivered edited work based on the clients' choices and specific requests.

I have also lead a photography crew of four people on multiple occasions to assist in lighting, posing, and equipment management.

Many of my works have received recognition: four front-page features on berkeley.edu, two Instagram features on UC Berkeley's Instagram (https://www.instagram.com/ucberkeleyofficial/), and two features on Southbay Photo's Instagram (https://www.instagram.com/southbay.photos/). Please see the featured content in my featured photos above and my photography portfolio on the URL below.

projects.title: Dungeon Generator (Java)
projects.description: I co-wrote a pseudo-random dungeon-generator game in Java that dynamically responds to user input through a graphical user interface (GUI), employs file-saving persistence to preserve and later resume the state of the game, and generates unique worlds based on the user’s inputted seed in the form of a long. I verified correctness with comprehensive JUnit tests, converting both sanity and edge cases.

projects.title: Solar System Simulator (Java)
projects.description:
I wrote a Java program that simulates simple Newtonian physics in a celestial body. The user has the choice of how many bodies they want, the mass of each body, the initial velocity, and the distance from the center of the x/y-coordinate system to the body. The sun in our solar system, for example, would have an initial position of  (x,y) = (0,0). We calculate the trajectories of the planets using F = (G)(m)(M)/(r^2), where r is the distance from the body to the origin. We then covert our calculated force into acceleration, find then new velocity, and apply that new velocity to determine the new position at a higher tilmestep. 

The program takes user input and validates it. The user also has the option of using the image of their choice. To preserve consistency, the program resizes all images of bodies to a resolution of 50x50 if it is not at the origin and 100x100 otherwise.

testScores.name: Elementary Spanish (Spanish 1) Cumulative Final Oral Exam at UC Berkeley
testScores.description: I earned the high score of 50/50 (class average: 45.9) on my cumulative final oral exam at Berkeley, which assessed a 12-minute-one-on-one interaction with a classmate based on an impromptu topic. Relevantly, I also earned the high score of 10/10 (class average: 7.2/10) and the high score score of 98/100 (class average: 84.4/100) on the semester-long assessments of oral proficiency and participation, respectively.

testScores.name: Elementary Spanish (Spanish 1) Cumulative Final Written Exam at UC Berkeley
testScores.description: I earned a score of 167/177 on my cumulative final exam at Berkeley (class average: 154.2/177), which assessed vocabulary relating to business interactions, interpersonal relationships, time, and other common vocabulary in the present tense (el tiempo presente), the future tense (el tiempo futuro en la forma de ir + a + infinitivo), and the past tense (el tiempo pretérito). In addition to the three tenses mentioned for necessary interactions in a Spanish-speaking environment, I was assessed on writing a 400-word essay on who I admire and why (I wrote about my mom).
